title: A novel mechanism of chlorogenic acid against type 2 diabetes-induced diabetic retinopathy: suppressing ferroptosis via NRF2/xCT/GPX4 and STAT3 signaling.
authors: Zheng, Jie; Wang, Xilong; Guo, Yiyuan; Feng, Lixia
one_liner_zh: 该文研究绿原酸通过NRF2/STAT3信号通路抑制铁死亡治疗糖尿病视网膜病变，虽含分子对接但核心是细胞信号通路与疾病机制，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a common microvascular complication of type 2 diabetes (T2D), driven by hyperglycemia-induced oxidative stress, ferroptosis, and inflammatory signaling. Here, we demonstrate that chlorogenic acid (CGA) ameliorates T2D and DR by simultaneously modulating the NRF2/xCT/GPX4 antioxidant pathway and the p-STAT3/xCT/GPX4 inflammatory-ferroptosis axis. High-fat diet (HFD) combined with streptozotocin (STZ)-induced T2D mice and high-glucose (HG)-stimulated human retinal microvascular endothelial cells (HRMECs) were used to evaluate the effects of CGA in vivo and in vitro. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, Western blotting, immunofluorescence, Seahorse metabolic assays, and site-directed mutagenesis were employed to investigate the underlying molecular mechanisms. CGA treatment significantly improved systemic metabolic parameters, including fasting blood glucose, HbA1c, and insulin sensitivity, while reducing anxiety-like behavior in T2D mice. Histological analyses revealed that CGA alleviated retinal structural abnormalities and decreased lipid droplet accumulation. Mechanistically, CGA activated NRF2/xCT/GPX4 signaling to enhance antioxidant defenses and suppress ferroptosis, while inhibiting STAT3 phosphorylation, reducing pro-inflammatory cytokines, and modulating xCT/GPX4 expression. In HRMECs, NRF2 inhibition or STAT3 activation attenuated CGA's protective effects, highlighting the critical roles of these pathways. Molecular docking and CETSA analyses further identified N485 of STAT3 as a key residue mediating CGA binding and functional regulation. These findings indicate that CGA exerts multi-modal protective effects against DR by targeting oxidative stress, ferroptosis, and inflammation. This study provides mechanistic insight into CGA as a potential therapeutic candidate for T2D-associated retinal complications and underscores the broader relevance of NRF2 and STAT3 pathways as intervention targets in diabetes-related microvascular disorders.
abstract_zh: 糖尿病视网膜病变（diabetic retinopathy, DR）是2型糖尿病（type 2 diabetes, T2D）常见的微血管并发症，由高血糖诱导的氧化应激、铁死亡（ferroptosis）和炎症信号驱动。在此，我们证明绿原酸（chlorogenic acid, CGA）通过同时调节NRF2/xCT/GPX4抗氧化通路和p-STAT3/xCT/GPX4炎症-铁死亡轴，改善T2D和DR。采用高脂饮食（high-fat diet, HFD）联合链脲佐菌素（streptozotocin, STZ）诱导的T2D小鼠和高糖（high-glucose, HG）刺激的人视网膜微血管内皮细胞（human retinal microvascular endothelial cells, HRMECs），在体内和体外评估CGA的效果。利用网络药理学、分子对接、Western blotting、免疫荧光、Seahorse代谢分析和定点突变技术，研究其潜在分子机制。CGA治疗显著改善了全身代谢参数，包括空腹血糖、HbA1c和胰岛素敏感性，同时减少了T2D小鼠的焦虑样行为。组织学分析显示，CGA减轻了视网膜结构异常并减少了脂滴积累。机制上，CGA激活NRF2/xCT/GPX4信号以增强抗氧化防御并抑制铁死亡，同时抑制STAT3磷酸化、减少促炎细胞因子，并调节xCT/GPX4表达。在HRMECs中，NRF2抑制或STAT3激活减弱了CGA的保护作用，凸显了这些通路的关键角色。分子对接和CETSA分析进一步鉴定STAT3的N485为介导CGA结合和功能调节的关键残基。这些发现表明，CGA通过靶向氧化应激、铁死亡和炎症，对DR发挥多模式保护作用。本研究为CGA作为T2D相关视网膜并发症的潜在治疗候选药物提供了机制性见解，并强调了NRF2和STAT3通路作为糖尿病相关微血管疾病干预靶点的更广泛相关性。
